parts.name: frame body

physics.Basic_description: The main structural component, appearing as a matte black, rigid C-shaped or bar-like frame made of injection-molded plastic.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the backbone structure that resists the clamping force and holds the fixed jaw and screw mechanism in alignment.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can firmly grasp the vertical spine or the horizontal arms of the frame to stabilize the tool during operation.
physics.reason: Injection molded plastic tools of this size typically use ribbed hollow shells to save material and weight while maintaining stiffness.

parts.description: The main structural component, appearing as a matte black, rigid C-shaped or bar-like frame made of injection-molded plastic.
parts.function: Provides the backbone structure that resists the clamping force and holds the fixed jaw and screw mechanism in alignment.

parts.name: anvil pad

physics.Basic_description: A grey, circular pad located at the tip of the fixed jaw, appearing softer than the surrounding frame.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a high-friction, non-marring surface to protect the workpiece from damage and prevent slippage.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a primary grasp target; touching this part would likely result in a slippery or compliant grip.
physics.reason: Small functional pads are typically solid molded rubber or TPE inserts.

parts.description: A grey, circular pad located at the tip of the fixed jaw, appearing softer than the surrounding frame.
parts.function: Provides a high-friction, non-marring surface to protect the workpiece from damage and prevent slippage.

parts.name: screw core

physics.Basic_description: A white/light grey cylindrical rod with threading, extending through the movable jaw assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Converts the rotational input from the handle into linear clamping force via the screw threads.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasping the threaded rod is not recommended as it interferes with the mechanism and offers poor friction.
physics.reason: Screw rods must be solid to transmit axial force without buckling.

parts.description: A white/light grey cylindrical rod with threading, extending through the movable jaw assembly.
parts.function: Converts the rotational input from the handle into linear clamping force via the screw threads.

parts.name: screw collar

physics.Basic_description: A small yellow ring or band located centrally on the screw assembly, likely a spacer or visual indicator.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as a stop, spacer, or wear ring within the screw mechanism assembly.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and recessed to be a viable grasp point for a standard gripper.
physics.reason: Small mechanical rings are typically solid or thick-walled enough to be treated as solid for physics.

parts.description: A small yellow ring or band located centrally on the screw assembly, likely a spacer or visual indicator.
parts.function: Acts as a stop, spacer, or wear ring within the screw mechanism assembly.

parts.name: swivel pad

physics.Basic_description: An orange circular pad at the tip of the screw, designed to contact the workpiece.
physics.Functional_description: Rotates independently of the screw to apply even pressure without twisting the workpiece surface.
physics.Grasped_description: Not suitable for grasping due to its small size and soft, high-friction material.
physics.reason: Like the anvil pad, this is a solid functional insert.

parts.description: An orange circular pad at the tip of the screw, designed to contact the workpiece.
parts.function: Rotates independently of the screw to apply even pressure without twisting the workpiece surface.

parts.name: lever hub

physics.Basic_description: A purple blocky component connecting the handle arms to the central screw mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Transfers torque from the handle arms to the screw core securely.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to rotate the screw, though the arms offer better leverage.
physics.reason: This is a high-stress connection point, likely solid or very thick-walled plastic.

parts.description: A purple blocky component connecting the handle arms to the central screw mechanism.
parts.function: Transfers torque from the handle arms to the screw core securely.

parts.name: lever arm

physics.Basic_description: Cyan-colored cylindrical rods extending upwards from the hub, forming the structure of the T-handle.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the lever arm length necessary to generate sufficient torque to tighten the clamp.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can grasp these rods to rotate the handle, preferably near the ends for maximum torque.
physics.reason: Thin cylindrical rods in handles are typically solid to resist bending moments.

parts.description: Cyan-colored cylindrical rods extending upwards from the hub, forming the structure of the T-handle.
parts.function: Provides the lever arm length necessary to generate sufficient torque to tighten the clamp.

parts.name: grip ridge 0

physics.Basic_description: Pink-colored horizontal rings or ridges encircling the lever grips, adding texture.
physics.Functional_description: Increases surface area and friction to prevent the hand or gripper from sliding along the handle axis.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasping here ensures positive locking against axial slip during rotation.
physics.reason: These are surface features (ridges) integral to the grip or added bands, effectively solid in the context of manipulation.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
